Do: Separate animated HUD/counters from static background/frames
Code Bad: One giant Canvas containing 50 elements where 1 changes every frame

Guideline: Disable Raycast Target on non-interactive elements
Don't: Leaving Raycast Target ON for everything
Code Bad: Text and decoration images with raycastTarget = true

Guideline: Apply juicy tactile feedback on button clicks
Description: Give game feel with scale tween and sound
Do: Punch scale ~1.1x and settle back to 1.0x on pointer down, kill the previous tween first so rapid taps never compound, and play SFX
Don't: Static button that just changes color or does nothing

Guideline: Handle Device Notch and Safe Area
Do: Use Safe Area helper script to clamp RectTransform
Code Bad: RectTransform anchor 0-1 on iPhone with Dynamic Island

Description: Keep drawcalls low and sharp borders
Do: Pack UI sprites into SpriteAtlas and set 9-slice borders on buttons
Don't: Raw uncompressed PNGs and scaled non-sliced images
Code Bad: Stretched non-sliced button with blurry corners

Guideline: Use TextMeshPro with SDF and Outlines
Description: Sharp text at any scale with game aesthetic
Do: Use TextMeshProUGUI with outline/underlay baked into a shared Material Preset (Unity 6: TMP ships inside com.unity.ugui)
Code Good: TextMeshProUGUI using shared material preset 'Title_Outline' (Outline 0.2 + Underlay)
Code Bad: Legacy UnityEngine.UI.Text; or tmp.fontMaterial.SetFloat(...) per label (creates a material instance and breaks batching)

Guideline: Modal Dialog Popup with Dimming Overlay
Description: Clear visual focus for game dialogs
Do: Modal popup with 60% black overlay and bounce-in animation
Don't: Dialog without dim background competing with game board
Code Bad: Dialog placed directly over active game board

Guideline: Limit UI DrawCalls (draw calls) to under 15 batches
Description: Prevent UI from dominating frame render budget
Do: Keep batching intact: group elements using the same material/atlas and avoid Z-order interleaving; check batch count in the Frame Debugger
Don't: Alternating text and images causing batch breaks
Code Bad: Image then Text then Image causing 20 batches

Do: Spawn pooling floating text with upward float and fade-out
Don't: Updating static text counter immediately without animation

Description: Prevent mis-taps on small phone screens
Do: With CanvasScaler reference width 1080 (~3x density), keep tappable rects >= 144x144 units (48dp; iOS 44pt = 132)
Don't: Tiny close buttons (64x64 units on a 1080-wide reference is only ~21dp)
Code Good: Button RectTransform sizeDelta >= (144, 144) at 1080x1920 reference resolution

Guideline: Set the CanvasScaler reference resolution for portrait games
Description: One canvas scaler layout from 16:9 and 21:9 phones to 3:4 tablets
Do: CanvasScaler: Scale With Screen Size, reference resolution 1080x1920, Screen Match Mode Expand so the reference area always fits (Match Width Or Height = 0 clips vertical content on 3:4 tablets); check 9:16, 9:21 and 3:4 in Device Simulator
Don't: Constant Pixel Size on a mobile game canvas
Code Good: canvasScaler.uiScaleMode = CanvasScaler.ScaleMode.ScaleWithScreenSize; canvasScaler.referenceResolution = new Vector2(1080, 1920); canvasScaler.screenMatchMode = CanvasScaler.ScreenMatchMode.Expand
Code Bad: Constant Pixel Size: buttons shrink on 1440p phones and overflow on 720p

Guideline: Pool ScrollRect list cells (scroll list pooling)
Description: Long shop/leaderboard scroll lists stay at 60 FPS without GC spikes
Do: Instantiate only the visible cells plus one spare row and recycle them while the ScrollRect scrolls; clip with RectMask2D
Don't: Instantiate one prefab per item (hundreds of cells) under a VerticalLayoutGroup + ContentSizeFitter
Code Good: Recycling pool of ~12 cells repositioned in onValueChanged of the ScrollRect
Code Bad: foreach (var item in items) Instantiate(cellPrefab, content)

Guideline: Hide a canvas with Canvas.enabled, not SetActive
Do: Disable the Canvas component (it stops issuing draw calls but keeps its vertex data, so showing it again needs no rebuild) and its GraphicRaycaster so hidden buttons cannot take taps
Don't: gameObject.SetActive(false/true) on a large panel every time it opens (OnDisable/OnEnable + full rebuild)

Guideline: Cut UI overdraw from invisible and full-screen images
Description: Fill rate is the GPU bottleneck on mobile UI
Do: Disable Images that are fully transparent: with Cull Transparent Mesh on (the default for new components) they skip drawing but still take raycasts and rebuild cost, and with it off they still render; avoid stacking full-screen panels and stop rendering the 3D scene behind an opaque full-screen menu; inspect with the Scene view Overdraw mode
Don't: Transparent full-screen Image used only as a click blocker or fade layer left enabled
Code Good: Disable the fade Image when the tween completes; camera.enabled = false behind an opaque full-screen menu
Code Bad: Image color alpha = 0 left active over the whole screen

Guideline: Debounce taps on purchase and reward buttons
Description: Stop double purchase / double reward claim from a fast double tap
Do: Set button.interactable = false on the first tap and restore it only after the action completes, with a cooldown of at least 1000 ms
Don't: Calling the purchase or claim logic on every onClick with no guard
Code Good: buyButton.interactable = false; try { await PurchaseAsync(); } finally { await Awaitable.WaitForSecondsAsync(1f); buyButton.interactable = true; }

Description: UI taps work when the project uses the Input System package
Do: Replace StandaloneInputModule with InputSystemUIInputModule on the EventSystem when Active Input Handling is Input System
Don't: Keeping StandaloneInputModule with Active Input Handling = Input System only (it throws and UI ignores taps)
Code Bad: EventSystem + StandaloneInputModule in an Input System-only project

Guideline: Place primary actions in the thumb zone of portrait games
Description: One-handed play: the main action is reachable without shifting grip
Do: Put play, buy and confirm buttons in the bottom third of the screen; keep rarely used actions (settings, close) at the top
Don't: Primary action button at the top of a portrait screen
Code Good: Play/Confirm anchored bottom-center above the safe area
Code Bad: Main CTA anchored to the top bar

Guideline: Avoid Layout Groups and Animators on dynamic UI
Description: Each change in a Layout Group dirties the whole chain; an Animator dirties its element every frame
Do: Use anchors for static layout, run a Layout Group once then disable it, and animate UI from code (tweens) instead of Animator
Don't: Nested HorizontalLayoutGroup/VerticalLayoutGroup/ContentSizeFitter on elements that change every frame
Code Good: layoutGroup.enabled = false after the first layout pass; tween scale/alpha in code
Code Bad: Animator on a static HUD panel; nested Layout Groups under a live score counter
